blocks.heading: Resume Is a One-Page Sales Document
rows: Know who decides
A recruiter scans first and a hiring manager checks later. The skills line must make sense to both: exact tool names for the recruiter, proof for the manager.
Name the problem you solve
Read the job post and find the three tasks it repeats. Your top skills should answer those three tasks, in the same words where true.
Show proof
One receipt line per core skill, plus one link to the work itself. A link beats a claim every time.
Make a clear ask
A headline that names the role you want, such as "Entry-level data analyst". A resume that asks for nothing gets nothing.
Follow up
After you apply, send one short note or ask for a referral. A resume that is never followed up works only as well as luck allows.

blocks.heading: How ATS and Recruiters Treat Skills
rows: Skills are the first thing recruiters filter on

In a Jobscan survey of 384 recruiters (February to March 2025), 76.4% said they start filtering by skills, and over 99.7% use filters in their ATS. It is a vendor survey, so treat it as a strong hint, not a law.
Keep a clearly labelled "Skills" heading and use exact tool names.
ATS software auto-rejects most resumes

The "75% rejected by a robot" figure has no clear source. In Enhancv interviews with 25 US recruiters (2025), 23 said their system does not auto-reject for formatting or content. Two did use match thresholds. The sample is small.
Do not panic about a bot. Do expect hard knock-out questions on things like degree, location or work authorisation.
More keywords means more chances

Greenhouse, an ATS maker, warns that leaning too hard on keyword filters can overlook qualified people because of mismatched wording. A human still reads the shortlist, and a copied keyword list fails there.
Use the words of the job post only for skills you can discuss.
Skill bars and star ratings are invisible to ATS
Resume-tool vendors say so, but none of the pages we read published a test. The safe, tested-by-you method: paste your resume into a plain text file and see what survives.
Write skills as plain text. Ratings are weak anyway, because nobody knows what "4 out of 5" means.
Recruiters read your resume for about seven seconds
The Ladders 2018 eye-tracking study reported 7.4 seconds for the first screen. A recruiter-industry critic points out it measures the quick keep-or-skip look, not the full review.
Put your target role and best proof in the top third. Treat clear layout as the real lesson.

blocks.heading: Tailor, Follow Up and Track One Number
rows: Applications sent
How many roles you applied to, and how many were a close fit.
Many applications with weak fit is spray and pray. Fewer, sharper applications are easier to learn from.
Replies
Replies of any kind: a call, an email, a test link, even a polite no.
Few replies usually point to role targeting, or to the top third of the resume not matching the post.
Interviews
Calls or meetings that came from your applications or referrals.
Good replies but few interviews often means the skills line has claims with no receipt.
Offers
Interviews that turned into an offer.
Interviews with no offers usually means you cannot yet explain your listed skills out loud.

blocks.heading: Receipt Line: Tool, Action, Checkable Output

items.text: Good knowledge of MS Excel.
Skills: communication, teamwork, MS Office, leadership.
Exact tools the post names, if you have used them (Excel, Tally, SQL, Figma, AutoCAD).
Working methods tied to an output (data cleaning, reconciliation, technical drawing, copywriting).
Languages you can actually work in, with an honest level in words.
One or two soft skills only where an example sits elsewhere on the page.

blocks.heading: Soft Skills and Communication in English

items.text: Good communication skills.
Team player.
Fluent in English.
Core skill: One language used in one deployed project
Multiplier skill: SQL, testing, or a domain such as finance or health
Proof shelf: GitHub repository with a README, plus a live link

blocks.heading: AI Skills on a Fresher Resume

items.text: AI tools: ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Midjourney.
Prompt engineering expert.
List every skill you could write.
Pick your three strongest and write a receipt line for each, using the pattern above.
Use the free Resume Skills Evidence Builder .
Put those three lines in the top third of your resume, then tailor the order for each job post.
Track applications, replies and interviews, and change only one thing at a time.
